items.title: Implement the split ledger: groups, share types and deterministic remainder
items.outcome: Groups, expenses and share allocations exist with a database-enforced sum constraint, and every share type allocates the last minor unit deterministically so dividing an amount that does not divide evenly never creates or destroys a minor unit.
items.context: Splitting is viral and is treated as acquisition rather than revenue, so it must be free and it must be correct. The correctness bar is arithmetic and is enforced by the database; authorization, settlement and erasure are a different risk surface and are a separate ticket.
scope: Group, membership, expense and share storage with a sum constraint enforced in the database
Share types covering equal, exact, percentage, shares and adjustment
Deterministic remainder allocation that is documented and reproducible
Placeholder members who are not users, with an atomic identity claim later
Free-tier entitlement so the full split journey completes without payment
Deterministic debt simplification per currency that minimizes settlement transfers without rewriting original obligations
Inspectable derivation from each proposed settlement back to original expenses and shares
acceptance_criteria: An unbalanced share set is rejected by the database, proven by a direct insert attempt
Dividing an amount that does not divide evenly allocates every minor unit deterministically and the same inputs always produce the same allocation
Every share type is property-tested against the sum constraint over generated inputs
A placeholder cannot read any other member data, and claiming an identity merges balances atomically
The full split journey completes on a free account, proven by an entitlement test
Simplification never mixes currencies and never changes an original expense, share or recorded settlement
The proposal uses no more transfers than the documented algorithm permits and is deterministic for tied balances
Every proposal carries a derivation that exactly reconciles to each member's original net balance
contracts_schema: Implements the published sharing contract including the stated sum constraint
Implements the published debt-simplification proposal and derivation shapes
security_privacy: Placeholder records hold the minimum identifying data needed to invite
A share allocation is stored rather than derived, so a later code change cannot silently restate a settled split
observability: Publishes group and expense counts and constraint violation attempts without amounts
Publishes proposal size and computation latency without member identities or amounts
tests: Property tests per share type over generated amounts
Property tests preserving every member net balance across simplification
Currency separation, tie-break determinism and original-record immutability tests
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag per cohort; disabling the flag hides creation while existing groups remain readable
Rollback never recomputes existing allocations, which are stored rather than derived
non_goals: Group authorization, settlement recording and counterparty erasure, which are their own ticket
Acting as a payment processor or holding funds, permanently
Client surfaces, which are the Android ticket
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the split schema and the allocation arithmetic only.

items.title: Implement split authorization, settlement recording and counterparty erasure
items.outcome: Group access is default deny and consistent with the sharing model, settlements are recorded without ever holding funds, and erasing one member leaves every other member balance correct and reconcilable.
items.context: The arithmetic is only half the problem. Who may read a group, what a settlement record is allowed to claim, and what happens to a shared balance when one party exercises erasure are authorization and privacy questions with their own reviewer and their own failure modes.
scope: Group authorization consistent with the sharing model, default deny
Atomic identity claim hardening so an invitation cannot be hijacked
Settlement recording and payment deep links, with no funds held
Counterparty erasure semantics as specified by the erasure decision record
Settlement and dispute notices are enqueued through the T-NOT-01 outbox and never carry an amount in the payload
acceptance_criteria: A hijacked claim attempt fails; the claim requires proof controlled by the invited person
Leaving a group removes access immediately and historically
Erasing one member leaves other member balances correct and reconcilable
Non-members are denied by default and membership is never inferred from an invitation
No settlement path holds funds at any point, proven by a code-level assertion
contracts_schema: Implements the published sharing contract settlement and revocation shapes
security_privacy: Non-members are denied by default; membership is never inferred from an invitation
Settlement deep links carry no amount in a way that a third party could alter meaningfully
observability: Publishes authorization denials, claim attempts and erasure reconciliation outcomes without amounts
tests: Assertion test proving no settlement path holds funds
rollout_rollback: Shipped with the split ledger flag; authorization is never behind its own flag
Rollback removes settlement recording and leaves balances readable
non_goals: Split schema and allocation arithmetic, which are their own ticket
Acting as a payment processor or holding funds, permanently
Client surfaces, which are the Android ticket
Notification delivery, scheduling, preferences and provider integration, which T-NOT-01 owns

items.title: Build the Android split experience with itemised bills, settlements and activation instrumentation
items.outcome: As a user, I can create a group, split a bill including item by item, invite someone who does not have the application, settle up through a payment link, and always see how a split was calculated.
items.context: The split flow is the acquisition surface, so friction and opacity both cost directly. Showing the derivation matters as much here as in the debt engine: a user who cannot see why they owe a particular amount will not trust the number or the application.
scope: Group creation, invitation and membership management
Expense entry with every supported share type
Itemised bill splitting that rolls up exactly to the expense total
Derivation view showing how each share was calculated including the remainder
Settlement recording with a payment deep link
Activation instrumentation from split participation to core usage
Debt-simplification proposal and derivation view with no client-side arithmetic
Split-dispute creation, status and resolution history
Group-scoped CSV and JSON history export with selection, progress, cancellation and expiry states
acceptance_criteria: An itemised split rolls up to exactly the expense total and the interface refuses to save otherwise
The derivation view explains the remainder allocation in plain language
Inviting someone without an account produces a working invitation and a visible placeholder
A settlement is recorded and the deep link opens the payment application without the application handling funds
Instrumentation payloads contain no monetary values, verified by the traffic capture harness
All split screens are screen-reader traversable and usable at the largest text scale
A user can trace every simplified settlement to original expenses and shares
A disputed share is visibly marked and its resolution is shown to every authorized member
Simplification and dispute journeys are screen-reader traversable and usable at the largest text scale
A group export reconciles to the displayed balances, excludes revoked-member private data and names its format version
contracts_schema: Consumes the published sharing contract; no share arithmetic is performed on the device
security_privacy: Invitation links expire and cannot be used to enumerate users
Group content is excluded from device backup and from crash reports
observability: Funnel events record step and outcome only, never amounts or member identities
tests: Instrumented split creation and settlement tests
Traffic capture assertion on instrumentation payloads
Group export balance reconciliation, revoked-member exclusion and expiry tests
rollout_rollback: Behind the same flag as the server feature, enabled per cohort
Rollback hides creation while existing groups stay readable
non_goals: Server allocation logic, which the api ticket owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo android. Owns the split feature module. All arithmetic stays on the server.

items.title: Implement the relationship-based authorization model with per-member, per-category grants
items.outcome: Sharing is expressed as explicit relationship tuples where a grant is always to one person for one category, aggregate and detail are separate permissions, and the absence of a grant denies.
items.context: Implemented naively, household sharing is a well-documented vector for financial abuse in intimate relationships. The controls that prevent it are structural: a grant to one person must never become a grant to the household, and seeing a total must never imply seeing the line items.
scope: Authorization model versioned in the repository with a migration path
Per-member, per-category grant creation and inspection
Aggregate and detail modelled as separate permissions rather than one permission with a flag
Fixed closed-period aggregate reads with immutable snapshot identifiers, no arbitrary ranges or exclusion filters, and per-viewer query budgets
Default deny with an explicit decision result for every check
Latency budget for authorization checks and a caching strategy that invalidates on revocation
Grant tuples projected into the row-level security session context by the trusted setter T-SEC-01 owns, so the decision point and the database predicate cannot disagree
Launch age policy enforced on invitation, membership and grant creation; launch defaults to adult-only unless a separately approved parental-consent program exists
acceptance_criteria: A grant to one member does not grant any other member, proven by a test
Holding an aggregate permission never returns line items, proven by an attempted detail read
Repeated, overlapping or subtractive aggregate queries cannot isolate a member or transaction; the service returns the stable snapshot or a typed suppression response
Absence of a grant denies, and an expired grant denies
The model is versioned and a model change is applied by a repeatable migration
Authorization checks meet the published latency budget under load
Every grant, change and denial writes an audit event
Every allow decision is backed by a satisfied database grant predicate: a test that returns allow from the model while the database predicate denies is a failure, not a warning
An under-age or unknown-eligibility account cannot be invited, added or granted access, and no placeholder membership bypasses that denial
contracts_schema: Implements the published sharing contract where aggregate and detail are distinct operations
security_privacy: The model is the sole authorization source; no endpoint implements its own sharing rule
Grant metadata reveals nothing about the content being shared
The authorization model never reads across users by escalating the database connection; it supplies the grant set the policy predicate evaluates
Age eligibility is evaluated server-side from the versioned policy T-CMP-04 publishes; a client assertion alone is never trusted
observability: Publishes check volume, denial rate and check latency
tests: Differencing attacks using rapid polling, overlapping windows, exclusion filters and known-self subtraction
Adult-only invitation, placeholder claim and grant denial tests
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag; with the flag off, all sharing checks deny, which is the safe state
Rollback denies rather than reverting to an older permissive model
non_goals: Revocation and transparency, which is a separate ticket
Client surfaces, which are the Android ticket
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the authorization model and its migrations. Every sharing consumer calls the same decision point.

items.title: Implement instant revocation, safe exit, access transparency and cross-user key access
items.outcome: A person can revoke any grant immediately and unilaterally with no approval and no reason, leaving is quiet and complete, every detail-level view is visible to the person whose data it was, and a grantee's ability to decrypt ends the moment the grant does.
items.context: These controls are the entire mitigation for the abuse risk in household sharing, and the audit is explicit that the epic must not ship with any of them descoped. The cryptographic half is also currently impossible: per-user keys have no cross-user read path at all.
scope: Unilateral revocation with no counterparty approval and no reason required
Historical access cut on revocation, not only future access
Safe exit that is quiet, immediate, and retains no cached copies
Access transparency log of every detail-level view, readable by the data subject and not deletable by the viewer
Cross-user key access implemented as the erasure and key decision record specifies
Revocation invalidating the grantee's decryption path
Offline lease expiry for shared reads: an offline client stops serving previously granted data once the published lease bound elapses
Grant, revocation and cross-user access notices are enqueued through the T-NOT-01 outbox and carry a pointer rather than the shared data itself
acceptance_criteria: Revocation takes effect within the published time and requires no counterparty action
After revocation the grantee cannot read historical records, proven by an attempted read
After revocation the grantee cannot decrypt previously readable content, proven cryptographically rather than by an authorization check alone
Leaving a group sends no notification describing the reason and retains no server-side cache of shared data
Every detail-level view appears in the data subject's transparency log and the viewer cannot delete or hide it
A grantee cannot see the transparency log of the person whose data they viewed
An airplane-mode test proves the client denies a shared read after the published offline lease bound elapses with no reachable server, rather than serving cached shared data indefinitely
Revocation takes effect on a connected client within the published online bound, measured from the successful revoke call to the first denied read
The published online and offline bounds are the numbers the tests assert; no test and no user-facing string claims revocation is immediate
contracts_schema: Implements the published transparency log and revocation shapes
security_privacy: Key access is audited on every use and revocation is recorded as a key event
Notifications about sharing changes must not become a coercion channel; content is minimal by design
Revocation is fail-closed offline: an expired lease denies, and the client never extends its own lease
observability: Publishes revocation counts, transparency log write volume and key access events
tests: Cryptographic revocation test proving decryption fails after revocation
Transparency log visibility and immutability tests
Quiet exit test asserting no notification content
Airplane-mode lease-expiry test: revoke while the client is offline, advance the clock past the lease bound and assert the shared read is denied
Connected revocation-latency test asserting the online bound
rollout_rollback: Ships with the authorization model; sharing cannot be enabled without it
Rollback disables sharing entirely rather than shipping partial controls
non_goals: Device-side cache eviction, which is the Android ticket
Notification delivery, scheduling, preferences and provider integration, which T-NOT-01 owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns revocation, transparency and the key access path. The Android ticket handles only device-side eviction.

items.title: Build Android family sharing with cached-data eviction and a coercive-control review
items.outcome: As a household member, I can share specific things with specific people, see who looked at what, revoke instantly, and leave without a scene, and once I revoke, nothing remains readable on the other person's device.
items.context: Server-side revocation is meaningless if the counterparty's phone still holds a readable copy. This ticket also carries the written review that every sharing screen is checked for surveillance affordances, which is the control the abuse risk actually depends on.
scope: Grant management interface, per person and per category, defaulting to aggregate
Access log surface showing who viewed what and when
Immediate revocation control that is easy to reach and does not ask for a reason
Discreet exit that produces no dramatic notification
Cached shared data eviction on revocation, by signal and by time-to-live
Written coercive-control review of every sharing screen
acceptance_criteria: Sharing defaults to aggregate and granting detail requires a separate, explicit action
After revocation, the counterparty device shows no shared data once the wipe signal or the time-to-live has elapsed, verified on a physical device
Revocation is reachable within a small number of taps and never requires stating a reason
Exit produces no notification that reveals why the person left
The written review records that no screen offers silent monitoring and that the exit path was walked end to end
All sharing screens are screen-reader traversable and usable at the largest text scale
contracts_schema: Consumes the published sharing and transparency contracts
security_privacy: Cached shared data is encrypted at rest and excluded from device backup
The wipe signal carries no content and cannot be used to infer what was shared
observability: Sharing events record action and outcome only, never member identity in analytics
tests: Coercive-control review walkthrough with a written outcome
rollout_rollback: Behind the server flag; the device feature cannot be enabled while server-side revocation is off
Rollback removes the sharing surface and triggers eviction on affected devices
non_goals: Server authorization and transparency, which the api tickets own
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo android. Owns the sharing surfaces and eviction. Enforcement stays on the server.

items.title: Build the web split-group experience with itemised bills, settlement and disputes
items.outcome: As a user, I can create a group, split a bill including item by item on the web, settle up through a payment link, raise and resolve a dispute over a share, see group debt simplified to the fewest settling payments, export the group's history, and always see how a split and its rounding remainder were calculated.
items.context: This mirrors T-SPL-02's Android split experience for the web shell and adds two capabilities the mobile ticket does not carry: a dispute flow for a contested share, and a debt-simplification view that nets multiple pairwise balances within a group into the fewest settling payments, both of which need the same visible-derivation discipline the split ledger already commits to in its remainder allocation.
scope: Group creation, invitation and membership management
Expense entry with every supported share type
Itemised bill splitting that rolls up exactly to the expense total
Derivation view showing how each share and the remainder were calculated
Settlement recording with a payment deep link
Dispute flow letting a member contest a share with a visible resolution outcome
Debt-simplification view netting group balances into the minimum number of settling payments
Export of group expense and settlement history
acceptance_criteria: An itemised split rolls up to exactly the expense total and the interface refuses to save otherwise
The derivation view explains the remainder allocation in plain language
A disputed share is flagged and its resolution is visible to every group member
The debt-simplification view nets balances into no more settling payments than the mathematical minimum for the group
The exported history reconciles exactly against the balances shown on screen
Keyboard-only and screen-reader users can complete every split action including dispute and export, and the surfaces remain readable and operable at two hundred percent text zoom
contracts_schema: Consumes the published sharing contract from T-CON-04; no share arithmetic or debt-simplification computation is performed in the browser
security_privacy: Group content is excluded from browser storage persisted beyond what the sharing model requires
Dispute content is visible only to members of the affected expense
Dispute and settlement notifications contain no monetary values
observability: Funnel and dispute-resolution events record step and outcome only, never amounts or member identities
tests: Browser-matrix compatibility test across the supported browser set
rollout_rollback: Behind the same flag as the server split feature, enabled per cohort
Rollback hides creation while existing groups stay readable
non_goals: Server allocation, authorization and settlement logic, which the api tickets own
Native mobile split surfaces, which the Android ticket owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo web. Owns the split feature module for the web shell. All arithmetic, authorization and debt-simplification computation stay on the server.

items.title: Build web family sharing with grant management, instant revocation and cached-data eviction
items.outcome: As a household member, I can share specific things with specific people on the web, choose per-member, per-category and detail-level grants, see who looked at what, revoke instantly without stating a reason, leave without a scene, and once I revoke, nothing remains readable in the browser that held it.
items.context: This mirrors T-FAM-03's Android controls for the web shell. Server-side revocation established by T-FAM-02 is meaningless if a browser tab or its cache still holds a readable copy, so this ticket carries the same cached-data eviction obligation and the same coercive-control review discipline the Android ticket already applies.
scope: Grant management interface, per person and per category, defaulting to aggregate
Access transparency log surface showing who viewed what and when
Immediate revocation control that is easy to reach and never asks for a reason
Discreet exit that produces no dramatic notification
Cached shared data eviction from browser storage on revocation and on session end
Written coercive-control review of every sharing screen for surveillance affordances
acceptance_criteria: Sharing defaults to aggregate and granting detail requires a separate, explicit action
After revocation the browser holds no readable shared data once the wipe signal is processed, verified by a test
Revocation is reachable within a small number of clicks and never requires stating a reason

The access log is visible to the data subject and cannot be hidden or deleted by the viewer
Keyboard-only and screen-reader users can complete every sharing action including revocation and exit, and the surfaces remain readable and operable at two hundred percent text zoom

security_privacy: Cached shared data is never written to unencrypted persistent browser storage and is cleared on revocation and on session end
The wipe signal carries no content and cannot be used to infer what was shared
observability: Sharing events record action and outcome only, never member identity in analytics
